messages:
Maya: heads-up — nightly perf job 03/17 showing intermittent softmax jitter after the new kernel routing changes. failing ~2% of runs for fp8-paged flash variant. logs attached from the job.
Liam: ugh, saw one failing eval too. is it numeric overflow or nondet ordering? :thinking:
Ashley: quick summary — the failure is tiny but reproducible for long-context chat tests (seq_len ~2048, batch 8). outputs differ enough to trigger our regen checks. repro script below.
Ashley: ```bash
# repro
python tests/repro_attention.py --model rlhf-small --kernel paged_flash_fp8 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --seed 42
# then diff tokens
``` 
Noah: can you paste the exact diff snippet? i want to check whether it's a small head collapse or full divergence.
Ashley: snippet:
Ashley: ```
expected: "... the agent responded with confidence."
actual:   "... the agent responded withÿconfidence."
# non-printable char and log prob delta ~3.2e-2
``` 
Devon: weird char. looks like numeric noise causing a token index shift. our softmax floor/clamp is currently at 1e-7 for fp8 path.
Maya: profiling shows a temp exp overflow in the paged kernel when qkv scale > 1.2 for some batches. KV prefetch and small micro-batches correlate with higher variance.
Liam: is the kernel doing any per-block scaling or compensation? we added a heuristics-based kernel switcher last week that jumps to paged_flash_fp8 when avg_seq > 512.
Ashley: yes, selector logic in runtime: if (seq > 512 && batch <= 16) choose paged_flash_fp8. no extra numeric stabilization.
Noah: two quick proposals: 1) add a tiny softmax input clamp (e.g., subtract max then cap to range) before exp for fp8 path; 2) route borderline cases to bf16 fused kernel.
Devon: we already do `x -= max(x)` but fp8 quant/noise may still underflow/overflow. clamp to [-30, 30] before exp helps in other runtimes.
Maya: agree — can we gate clamp behind a runtime flag and A/B it in canary to measure perf impact? Concern: clamp adds one branch per tile, might hit latency SLO.
Liam: we can use a fast vectorized clamp in the CUDA kernel (no branch) so perf hit is negligible. ashley, can you prototype and bench?
Ashley: will try. also adding quick metrics from the job: p99 tail jumps from 18ms to 36ms for paged_flash_fp8 under this pattern, but bf16 fused stays ~20ms.
Noah: that suggests numerical instability triggers expensive fallback or re-computation path somewhere.
Maya: logs show a kernel selector hysteresis flip: several requests flip between paged and fused variant mid-rollout which amplifies cache churn and KV re-prefetches.
Devon: oh! that could explain higher variance: KV cache warmup + switching causes different memory layout -> different accumulation order -> tiny FP differences -> token drift.
Liam: so two levers: increase kernel selector hysteresis (e.g., require sustained metric for 5s before switch) and add numeric clamp for fp8.
Ashley: prototype patch: added `softmax_clamp = min(max(x - max_x, -LOG_LIMIT), LOG_LIMIT)` with LOG_LIMIT = 30 for fp8 path. small change, compile-test next.
Maya: great. can we also add a quick diag in runtime to record when selector flips per-request (small counter) so we can correlate with failing traces?
Noah: i can add a lightweight per-model metric: `kernel_flips/sec` and `kv_prefetches/sec` exported to console. then run nightly with diag enabled for 24h.
Liam: team, if the clamp + hysteresis reduces failing runs to <0.1% we can promote. otherwise we may need to force-route critical customers to bf16.
Devon: note: BF16 path increases mem by ~8% and latency ~1.1x. cost trade-off for correctness.
Ashley: ran local bench of clamp (vectorized) — microbench shows ~+0.5% latency for kernel, p99 stable. pushing patch to branch `attn-softmax-clamp`.
Maya: awesome. can we gate the canary rollout to 5% traffic and watch regen-evals for 6h?
Liam: @runbook-bot can you create canary job and link the CI/infra job ids? :pray:
runbook-bot: created canary deploy job 52177. CI perf job 52178 linked: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/52178. Observability flags: enable `attn:softmax_clamp` + `selector_hysteresis=5s` for canary.
Maya: thanks. i'll kick off the canary and follow up with regression stats.
Noah: also adding a short-term test: synthetic feed that toggles batch size/seq pattern to force flips. should reveal flaky patterns quickly.
Ashley: will post bench results here when available. if we still see drift, next step is to add exp-safe code path in kernel (use `expm1`-style numerics) or fall back to bf16 for affected models.
Liam: good plan. nice sleuthing everyone. :shipit:
Maya: quick action items:
Maya: - Ashley: PR for clamp + unit tests
Maya: - Noah: metrics for kernel flips + KV prefetch
Maya: - Liam: schedule canary 5% and rollback plan
Maya: - Devon: update selector config to 5s hysteresis
Maya: i'll monitor regen-evals and post results in 6h.
Ashley: on it. ```
